Assignment Title: Robot Task System — Overriding and Polymorphism

Assignment Question:
A warehouse deploys different types of robots. Every robot has a base power rating, but different robot types calculate their task performance differently. Some robots may also have abilities specific to their robot type.
Design a Java program using the following class hierarchy:
     Robot
      /  \
     /    \
CleaningRobot  SecurityRobot
The Robot class should store the robot's name and base power. It should provide a method to calculate the performance rating and a method to display the robot's name. The name-display method must not be overridden by subclasses.
The CleaningRobot class should inherit from Robot and override the performance calculation. A cleaning robot's performance is:
Performance = Base Power × 1.5
The SecurityRobot class should inherit from Robot, store the alert level, and override the performance calculation:
• If alert level is 8 or more: Performance = Base Power + 40 • Otherwise: Performance = Base Power
The SecurityRobot class should also provide a special alarm ability. It should return "Alarm triggered!" when the alert level is at least 8; otherwise, it should return "No alarm needed."
Create the appropriate robot object and store it using a common Robot reference. Use the reference to display the robot name and calculate the performance rating, demonstrating upcasting, method overriding, and dynamic method dispatch.
If the robot is a SecurityRobot, use downcasting to access the security-specific alarm ability.
The program should demonstrate method overriding, final methods, upcasting, downcasting, and runtime polymorphism.
Input Format
The input consists of:
• Line 1: Robot type (Cleaning or Security) • Line 2: Robot name • Line 3: Base power • Line 4: Alert level, only for a SecurityRobot
Constraints
• Robot type must be Cleaning or Security. • Robot name must be non-empty and must not contain numeric characters. • Base power must be positive. • For a SecurityRobot, alert level must be zero or greater. • Numeric inputs must be valid.
Output Format
For a valid CleaningRobot:
Robot: <name>
Performance: <performance>
For a valid SecurityRobot:
Robot: <name>
Performance: <performance>
<alarm result>
For invalid input:
Invalid Input
Sample Test Case 1
Input:
Cleaning
Robo
20
Output:
Robot: Robo
Performance: 30.0
